review_request: Parent-delivered union of independent C01 findings F1, F2, F3 and J2 additional; no private evaluation materials accessed.

changes.reason: Limit Tokio feature claims to the explicit dependency requests; the manifest does not establish the resolved feature union.

fields.before: Defines the internal Rust host crate and its permitted runtime surfaces.
fields.after: Defines the internal Rust host crate's package metadata and requested dependency features.

fields.before: Runtime Tokio enables threads, synchronization, time, I/O and networking, with no process feature; OS bindings are selected by cfg.
fields.after: This manifest requests Tokio rt-multi-thread, sync, time, io-util and net without explicitly requesting process; OS bindings are selected by cfg.

fields.before: Host process creation belongs to the supervisor; this manifest does not enable tokio::process.
fields.after: The listed Tokio features are this manifest's explicit requests, not a statement of Cargo's resolved feature union.

fields.before: Inherited versions cannot be established from this manifest alone.
fields.after: Inherited versions and the resolved Cargo feature union cannot be established from this manifest alone.

supporting_evidence.quote:
[dependencies]
omni-proto.workspace = true
tokio = { workspace = true, features = ["rt-multi-thread", "sync", "time", "io-util", "net"] }
tokio-util.workspace = true
sysinfo.workspace = true

[target.'cfg(unix)'.dependencies]
libc.workspace = true

[dev-dependencies]
serde.workspace = true
serde_json.workspace = true
regex.workspace = true
tokio = { workspace = true, features = ["macros", "rt-multi-thread", "time"] }

[lints]
workspace = true

changes.reason: Replace absolute identity-safe termination with identity-checked termination and distinguish missing-identity abandonment from the documented macOS check-to-signal PID-reuse interval.

fields.before: client platform Chan provides close and identity-safe termination.
fields.after: The platform Chan provides close and identity-checked termination; Unix identity checks are implemented in client/keeper.rs.

before: When supervisor identity cannot be checked, failure explicitly reports possible abandonment rather than risking a reused PID.
after: When required supervisor identity is unavailable, generation failure reports possible abandonment and the keeper declines to signal.
Distinct from abandonment, macOS keeper.rs checks the exit watch and start time then signals the PID; its documented check-to-signal interval can still permit PID reuse (lines 229–244).

changes.reason: Limit the PID-guard claim to request submission; forget mutates local state without a guard inside that method.

fields.before: A generation is bound to the host PID; inherited handles fail before mutation after fork.
fields.after: Request submission checks the host PID through home() before incrementing its request ID or mutating request state; forget() directly removes a local tree entry without its own home check.

changes.reason: Separate collection input bytes from output limits; Options has input data but no input-size-limit field.

fields.before: Collection input/output limits, cancellation, text decoding and pipe backpressure live in process Options rather than the wire request.
fields.after: Run input data, per-stream output limits, cancellation, text decoding and pipe backpressure live in process Options rather than the wire request; Options has no input-size-limit field.

acceptance: Pending independent review; documentary checks do not constitute self-approval.
